newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Ecuador to offer 36,000 bpd Oriente crude oil.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador to offer 36,000 bpd Oriente crude oil.

text.p: Ecuador's state oil company Petroecuador is planning to offer contracts for 36,000 barrels per day (bpd) of Oriente crude within the next seven days, an Ecuadorean government source said.
The tender volume used to be contracted to Mexico's Pemex International with 24,000 bpd and Totisa, a subsidiary of Tripetrol, with 12,000 bpd, but these contracts expired, he added.

The tender will be open to registered customers of Petroecuador and will be awarded to the bidder with the highest premium to the "invoice price formula", which is currently WTI - $5.60 on the U.S. Gulf Coast and ANS -$2.56 on the U.S. West coast.

The crude loads at the Pacific port of Balao/Esmeraldas, and would probably be awarded to a client on the American continent, the source said. The density of Oriente crude has been falling steadily over the past few years, and now stands at 25.5 API.
